sources.source: Littmann 1913, Deutsche Aksum-Expedition IV, inscription 11, pp.32–33, line11
sources.access: Downloaded scan; inspected p.33 and OCR p.32 dating circa350CE
sources.finding: Royal messengers/envoys; secular application. Strong evidence for pre-Quranic noun, not apostles or borrowing route.

Supports Ethiopic borrowing, cites inscription and Ethiopic Mark6:30; route via returnees from Abyssinia is conjecture, not adopted. Verse attributed to Dabi not independently dated; not used as pre-Quranic proof.
Explicitly classifies hawariyyun among Geʿez borrowings. Used as scholarly judgment, not documentary proof of transfer route.
Geʿez noun and traditional alternatives. Separate theological thesis about disciples not adopted as lexical evidence.
Agent noun related to hora go; cites Leslau249. Leslau page not directly obtained; citation is indirect and labeled so.

sources.access: Primary page not obtained; cited through Jeffery, Reynolds, Dost. Not counted as an independently inspected source.

sources.finding: Different naming accounts are later reports, not independent contemporary evidence for the occupations of Jesus disciples.
GarimaII parchment390–570CE, GarimaI530–660CE; manuscript antiquity not direct verification of hawarya in a specified early leaf.

sources.source: F.A.Bishi, Debunking the Ethiopic Loanword Claim, online draft
sources.access: Read opposing argument; publication/peer-review not established
sources.finding: Shared root/Arabic morphology do not disprove borrowing of a specific title. Inscription lead independently checked in Littmann; Safaitic readings and claimed Garima lexical witness not independently confirmed and not published as facts.

sources.source: Quranic Arabic Corpus Hwr + canonical local Arabic verses
sources.finding: Five occurrences:3:52:12;5:111:4;5:112:3;61:14:12;61:14:18. Classified root total13 does not establish historical derivation.

evidence_grades.strong: Fourth-century inscription for royal envoys; five Quranic occurrences and their contexts.
evidence_grades.well_supported_hypothesis: Geʿez borrowing, supported by specialized lexical usage and scholarly analyses; exact route/date unestablished.
evidence_grades.unverified_here: Specific pre-Quranic Christian manuscript occurrence of the noun; Leslau249 and Nöldeke48 primary pages.
evidence_grades.not_established: Clothing occupation as historical cause; inferring Quranic Messenger status from foreign etymology.
